title: TWINSPAN with ecan
text: TWINSPAN (Two-Way INdicator SPecies ANalysis, Hill 1979) classifies community data table way vegetation scientist arranges hand: splits stands two groups , names species best indicate split. stands species classified, hence two-way. ecan implements plain R, compiler needed. port Hill’s original FORTRAN program; ?twinspan lists known differences.
code: data(dune, package = "vegan") tw <- twinspan(dune) tw #> TWINSPAN #>   stands:       20 #>   pseudospecies: 75  #>   cut levels:   0 2 5 10 20 #>   divisions:    6 #>   groups:       7 #>  #> division 1 at level 0 (n = 20, eig = 0.511) #>   indicators: Ranuflam_1(+) Agrostol_1(+) Eleopalu_1(+) Lolipere_1(-) #> division 2 at level 1 (n = 13, eig = 0.384) #>   indicators: Hyporadi_1(-) #> division 3 at level 1 (n = 7, eig = 0.411) #>   indicators: Sagiproc_1(-) #> division 4 at level 2 (n = 10, eig = 0.317) #>   indicators: Planlanc_1(-) #> division 5 at level 3 (n = 5, eig = 0.284) #>   indicators: Achimill_1(+) #> division 6 at level 3 (n = 5, eig = 0.301) #>   indicators: Juncarti_1(+)

title: TWINSPAN with ecan
text: division made three steps. 1. Pseudospecies. TWINSPAN works presence absence, quantitative table first cut binary pseudospecies cut levels (default 0, 2, 5, 10, 20). species cover 7 present levels 1, 2 3, 4 5. 2. Primary ordination. first axis correspondence analysis pseudospecies found reciprocal averaging, stands divided centroid. 3. Refined indicator ordination. division polished using species prefer one side . preference runs -1 (negative group) 1 (positive group), pseudospecies differential absolute preference reaches diff_threshold (1/3 default, frequency ratio 2:1). Finally preferential pseudospecies chosen indicators, summarise division without defining . indicators every division shown print(), together eigenvalue axis made division (see output ).
code: psp <- pseudospecies(dune) dim(psp) #> [1] 20 75 head(colnames(psp)) #> [1] "Achimill_1" "Agrostol_1" "Airaprae_1" "Alopgeni_1" "Anthodor_1" #> [6] "Bellpere_1" ra <- tw_ra(psp) ra$eig #> [1] 0.5403802 pos <- ra$sample > 0 pref <- tw_preference(psp, pos) head(sort(pref)) #> Achimill_1 Airaprae_1 Anthodor_1 Bellpere_1 Bromhord_1 Cirsarve_1  #>         -1         -1         -1         -1         -1         -1

title: TWINSPAN with ecan
text: result gives one row per stand, group binary path divisions led . division tree becomes hclust object, clustering helpers ecan usual plotting functions can used.
code: head(tw$classification) #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   stand group path  depth #>   <chr> <int> <chr> <int> #> 1 11        1 00        2 #> 2 17        1 00        2 #> 3 19        1 00        2 #> 4 18        2 0100      4 #> 5 5         3 0101      4 #> 6 6         3 0101      4 table(tw$classification$group) #>  #> 1 2 3 4 5 6 7  #> 3 1 4 4 1 3 4 cls <- stats::as.hclust(tw) plot(cls, hang = -1, main = "TWINSPAN", xlab = "", sub = "")

title: TWINSPAN with ecan
text: original TWINSPAN divides every group level going deeper, groups level can differ widely heterogeneous . Roleček et al. (2009) instead divide heterogeneous group first, makes resulting groups comparable. ecan measures heterogeneity total inertia group. n_clusters number groups chosen directly, original hierarchy .
code: tw_inertia(psp) #> [1] 2.500848 tw_mod <- twinspan(dune, modified = TRUE, n_clusters = 4) table(tw_mod$classification$group) #>  #>  1  2  3  4  #>  3 10  3  4

title: Two-way indicator species analysis (TWINSPAN) — twinspan
text: x community data matrix data.frame. rownames: stands, colnames: species. cut_levels numeric vector pseudospecies cut levels. min_size integer. Groups smaller divided. max_depth integer maximum number division levels. default (6) original TWINSPAN (levmax). max_indicators integer maximum number indicator pseudospecies used summarise division. diff_threshold numeric (0, 1]. pseudospecies differential species absolute value preference less . default (1/3) corresponds 2:1 frequency ratio. refine_iter integer maximum number refinement steps. modified logical. TRUE: modified TWINSPAN. heterogeneous group divided first. n_clusters integer number groups stop , NULL limit. use_indicator logical. TRUE: use indicator ordination final division (original TWINSPAN). FALSE: use refined ordination. downweight logical. TRUE (default, original TWINSPAN): downweight rare pseudospecies ordination, way decorana(). See tw_downweight(). polish string. "hill" (default): divide way original TWINSPAN. "ecan": earlier way package. diff_threshold, refine_iter use_indicator used "ecan". species logical. TRUE: classify pseudospecies well stands, needed tw_two_way(). ... Ignored.
